title: Regex Power
description: Patterns that do the work a macro can't: very magic, groups and backreferences, zero-width matches, lazy repeats and lookaround.

levels.title: Expected goes first
levels.description: This test suite passes (actual, expected), but assert_eq wants (expected, actual). Swap the arguments of every assert_eq, and leave one space after each comma. round() stays as it is.
levels.hint: After \v, ( ) + and friends need no backslash. Capture each argument with (\S*), and bring them back as \2 and \1.

levels.title: Fence the constants
levels.description: The docs mention constants as plain text. Wrap every ALL_CAPS name of two or more letters in backticks. JavaScript and the word A are not constants.
start_text: A request fails after MAX_RETRIES attempts or TIMEOUT seconds.
Set API_KEY first, or JavaScript clients get a 401.
A missing BASE_URL falls back to DEFAULT_HOST and DEFAULT_PORT.

value: A request fails after `MAX_RETRIES` attempts or `TIMEOUT` seconds.
Set `API_KEY` first, or JavaScript clients get a 401.
A missing `BASE_URL` falls back to `DEFAULT_HOST` and `DEFAULT_PORT`.

levels.hint: & in the replacement stands for the whole match, so no group is needed. \u is any capital, so one capital followed by more of [A-Z_] skips the word A.

levels.title: Editor's stutter
levels.description: Remove every doubled word, keeping one copy. Careful: 'this is' and 'the theory' are not doubled words.
start_text: I think this is the the theory behind it,
and and it works if if you squint at at it.
The The bug is that this is is not tested.
We know the theory holds holds up.

value: I think this is the theory behind it,
and it works if you squint at it.
The bug is that this is not tested.
We know the theory holds up.

levels.hint: A backreference works inside the pattern too: (\w+) \1 is a word, then itself. In very magic mode, < and > mark word edges.

levels.title: Const correctness
levels.description: Nothing here is ever reassigned. Turn every let and var keyword into const. outlet, letter, variable, val and len keep their names.
start_text: let outlet = open(); var letter = outlet.read()
var val = letter.trim(); let len = val.length
var variable = len * 2; let done = true

value: const outlet = open(); const letter = outlet.read()
const val = letter.trim(); const len = val.length
const variable = len * 2; const done = true

levels.hint: In very magic mode, (a|b) matches either one. Word edges keep outlet and letter safe.

levels.title: Title case
levels.description: Capitalize every word of the Markdown headings. The body text stays lowercase.
start_text: some people still use the arrow keys.
the mouse is far away from home row.

value: some people still use the arrow keys.
the mouse is far away from home row.

levels.hint: \u in the replacement capitalizes the next character. :g picks the heading lines, and \< finds the start of each word.

levels.title: The last comma
levels.description: Lists read better with 'and': replace the last comma of each line with ' and'. Only the last one, and a line with no commas stays put.
start_text: Bugs: off-by-one, null, race, cache, naming

value: Tools: hammer, nails, glue and tape
Bugs: off-by-one, null, race, cache and naming

levels.hint: \zs says where the match really starts. Everything before it must still match, but isn't replaced, and .* is greedy.

levels.title: Thousands
levels.description: Nobody can read these sizes. Add a comma every three digits, counted from the right. Short numbers don't need one.
levels.hint: \ze says where the match really ends. Match one digit that has groups of three digits between it and the end of the number, and replace it with itself plus a comma.

levels.title: Uncommented
levels.description: Delete every block comment and the space before it. Comments can hold * and / of their own, there can be two on a line, and the division stays.
start_text: int ratio /* w/h */ = 2; int depth /* not used */ = 0;
int area /* w * h, see a/b.c */ = 80; /* in cm */
levels.hint: .\{-} is .* that takes as little as it can. Any character can delimit :s, so :s#a/b#c# saves escaping the slashes.

levels.title: Secure by default
levels.description: Move every http:// URL to https://, except the ones on localhost. login.example.com and local.example.com are real hosts, ftp stays ftp, and https is already fine.
levels.hint: X@! in very magic mode means 'not followed by X', and it consumes nothing. The lines mix URLs, so :g can't sort them out.

levels.title: Print statement
levels.description: Replace every bare print with log. Methods stay: self.print and buffer.print are someone else's problem.
levels.hint: X\@<! means 'not preceded by X', and it consumes nothing. \zs can't do this: it can only ask for what is there.
